editorial:
Imagine living your whole life believing that if you have a good day, someone else has to have a bad one. That is exactly how Edgar Lunt operates. He treats life like a math problem where every joy must be balanced by some kind of pain. It makes him a pretty miserable guy to be around, but he thinks he is just being logical. Then comes Trevor, a young student who is basically the opposite of Edgar. Trevor is full of energy and wants to push Edgar out of his shell. The vibe of the movie is a quiet, character-driven story about two people from totally different worlds trying to understand each other.

You will really appreciate the acting here because the chemistry between the grumpy older man and the hopeful student feels very real. The pacing is slow, which might bore some people, but it gives you time to actually care about Edgar's change of heart. If you enjoy stories about unlikely friendships, you should definitely give this a go.
endingExplained: By the end, Trevor successfully breaks through Edgar's walls. Edgar realizes that his scientific rule about balance was just an excuse to be afraid of being happy. He finally stops worrying about who is suffering and accepts that it is okay to enjoy life. The movie wraps up with Edgar becoming a much softer, kinder person who is open to the world, proving that a little bit of friendship can change a person's entire outlook.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about unlikely friendships and personal growth.
